The must-sees

12 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Bridge · 1966

    25 de Abril Bridge

    It opened in 1966 as the Salazar Bridge, named after the dictator. After the Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974 it was renamed after the date.

    Look for

    On the far bank, Cristo Rei stands with open arms on a tall pedestal, a statue inspired by Rio’s Christ the Redeemer.

  2. 02
    Neighbourhood

    Alfama

    It is the oldest district of Lisbon, and its rock foundations helped it survive the 1755 earthquake. It is closely tied to fado, Lisbon’s song of longing.

    Look for

    At the Santa Luzia viewpoint, tile panels show Praça do Comércio as it looked before the 1755 earthquake.

  3. 03
    Fortress

    Belém Tower

    Built in the early 16th century under King Manuel I, it guarded the river approach to Lisbon. Ships setting out on voyages of discovery sailed past it.

  4. 04
    Museum · 1969

    Calouste Gulbenkian Museum

    Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate, spent his last years in Lisbon and left his collection to a foundation. The museum opened in 1969, with art from ancient Egypt to Lalique jewellery.

    Look for

    Among the Lalique jewellery, find the Dragonfly Woman: a woman’s body ending in a dragonfly, with enamelled wings and claws.

  5. 05
    Church

    Jerónimos Monastery

    Manuel I founded it in 1501, paid for largely by spice-trade wealth. Vasco da Gama’s tomb lies inside the church, and the poets Luís de Camões and Fernando Pessoa are also commemorated here.

    Look for

    On the south portal facing the road, Henry the Navigator stands on the pillar between the two doors.

  6. 06
    Church

    Lisbon Cathedral

    Building began in the 12th century, soon after Afonso Henriques took Lisbon from the Moors in 1147. Excavations in the cloister show Roman and Moorish remains.

    Look for

    Between the two towers, a large rose window sits above the main door.

  7. 07
    Museum · 1998

    Lisbon Oceanarium

    Designed by Peter Chermayeff for Expo 98, it shows ocean habitats around a single big tank seen from many angles. It is one of the largest aquariums in Europe.

  8. 08
    Landmark · 1960

    Monument to the Discoveries

    A temporary version was made for the 1940 Portuguese World Exhibition, and this stone one was built in 1960, 500 years after Henry’s death. A large compass-rose map is set into the pavement in front.

    Look for

    Henry stands at the prow holding a small caravel. Behind him come navigators, monks, soldiers and the poet Camões.

  9. 09
    Square

    Praça do Comércio

    The royal palace stood here until the 1755 earthquake and tsunami destroyed it. In 1908 King Carlos I and his heir were shot dead on the square, two years before Portugal became a republic.

    Look for

    At the water’s edge, marble steps run down into the river between two columns: the Cais das Colunas, the old royal landing.

  10. 10
    Square

    Rossio Square

    The column carries King Pedro IV, who was also Brazil’s first emperor. The National Theatre D. Maria II on the north side stands where the Inquisition’s palace once was.

    Look for

    Just off the north-west corner, Rossio station has a carved façade with two horseshoe-arched doorways.

  11. 11
    Station · 1902

    Santa Justa Lift

    It opened in 1902, designed by Raoul Mesnier du Ponsard. A walkway at the top leads across to the ruins of the Carmo Convent.

  12. 12
    Fortress

    São Jorge Castle

    The fortifications go back to the Moorish period. After Afonso Henriques captured Lisbon in 1147 the castle became a royal residence.

    Look for

    From the walls, look downriver for the red 25 de Abril Bridge and the Cristo Rei statue on the far bank.
